articles.title: Voice AI in Advertising: Creating Dynamic Audio Ads
articles.excerpt: Why Voice AI is a Game‑Changer for Audio Advertising If you’ve ever tuned into a podcast or a streaming service and heard a perfectly‑timed, human‑sounding ad that seemed to know exactly what you need…
articles.body: Why Voice AI is a Game‑Changer for Audio Advertising If you’ve ever tuned into a podcast or a streaming service and heard a perfectly‑timed, human‑sounding ad that seemed to know exactly what you needed, you’ve already experienced the power of voice AI. Traditional radio spots are static—once recorded, they can’t adapt to the listener’s context, location, or even the time of day. Voice AI flips that script by letting developers generate dynamic, personalized audio ads on the fly . With text‑to‑speech (TTS) models that sound almost indistinguishable from real people, you can: Swap out product names, prices, or promotions in milliseconds. Match the tone to the brand’s personality —from conversational and upbeat to calm and authoritative.

articles.body: An agent that joins my tracker reads one URL: /llms-full.txt . It is 6,245 lines of Markdown, and I wrote about 1,800 of them. The rest is generated from the code, and the deploy refuses to ship a copy that has drifted from it. The constraint: an agent should need one page, not a tour of the docs site, and that page can't be a second copy of the truth that rots the week after it's written. I'm Panth, and I lead the software team at Oizom. This is from ticket-tracker , my open-source board, which my own agents work from. Section O of its agent plan is titled "One page an orchestrator can be pointed at". This post is how that page is built.

articles.title: How to choose a stock market data MCP server for AI agents: 9 checks I run first
articles.excerpt: The checks below work on any server. Under each one I've put Equibles' answers (and gaps) as a worked example. There are a lot of "best MCP servers for stock market data" lists now. Most of them compa…
articles.body: The checks below work on any server. Under each one I've put Equibles' answers (and gaps) as a worked example. There are a lot of "best MCP servers for stock market data" lists now. Most of them compare tool counts and prices. Those matter, but they're not what breaks when an AI agent starts answering money questions. What breaks is a number with no source, a quarter that's off by one, or an agent quietly answering from memory because the tool came back empty. So here are the nine checks I run before I trust a financial data MCP server with an agent. Each one takes a couple of minutes. 1. Can you click through to the source? Ask for one specific figure and see whether the answer comes with a link to the filing, and ideally the line.

articles.title: Securing AI-Driven Database Access with db-mcp-gateway
articles.excerpt: Securing AI-Driven Database Access with db-mcp-gateway In environments where AI agents need to query production databases, exposing credentials is a major risk. The db-mcp-gateway addresses this by ac…
articles.body: Securing AI-Driven Database Access with db-mcp-gateway In environments where AI agents need to query production databases, exposing credentials is a major risk. The db-mcp-gateway addresses this by acting as a self-hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) gateway that isolates credentials and enforces strict access controls. Credential Isolation All database passwords and connection strings reside only inside the gateway container. AI agents send queries through the MCP protocol and receive only result sets. No log line, error message, or response ever contains a URL or password, eliminating accidental leaks. Identity & Access Control Authentication is delegated to enterprise SSO providers such as Okta, Google Workspace, Entra, Authentik, and Keycloak.

articles.title: Coordinate Clicks Are a Trap: Driving a GUI Agent Without Pixel Guessing
articles.excerpt: The first version of my GUI agent clicked by pixel coordinates. It worked in demos and failed constantly in practice, and the reason is boring: pixels do not move, but content does. Here is what I cha…
articles.body: The first version of my GUI agent clicked by pixel coordinates. It worked in demos and failed constantly in practice, and the reason is boring: pixels do not move, but content does. Here is what I changed, in order of impact. 1. Read the tree before you click Both desktop and mobile expose an accessibility tree: uiautomator dump on Android, UI Automation on Windows, the accessibility APIs on macOS. Nodes come with labels, roles and bounds. Clicking the node whose text is "Send" survives a re-layout; clicking (984, 183) does not. The tree is not a luxury. It is the difference between an agent that works on your machine and an agent that only works on the screenshot you tuned it against. 2.

articles.title: A canary you keep is a canary you start trusting
articles.excerpt: A reader named Zhang Enquan came back to a thing I wrote about green builds. He had run 10,000 real prompts through a tokenizer, and the first thing he checked was not the output. It was whether every…
articles.body: A reader named Zhang Enquan came back to a thing I wrote about green builds. He had run 10,000 real prompts through a tokenizer, and the first thing he checked was not the output. It was whether every sample actually entered the pipeline. 40.5% of individual items were off by more than 20%. The batch looked about 5% off. The errors were not on top of the average. They were inside it, where nobody looks. Which is how a suite lies without ever going red. Averaging is a very polite way to lose the tail. He also said the part I keep: re-deriving the canary is cheaper than it sounds. His canary is one known prompt whose token count he can check by hand. Recomputing it every run costs seconds and catches the thing a cached fixture cannot, which is the pipeline quietly skipping samples.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 20, 1970: The Soviet Union launches last-ever Zond moon mission
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. This was the last mission in the Zond program. After the first three Zond missions explored Venus and Mars , the next ones were circumlunar missions that flew around the moon before returning to Earth. Although there was no crew on board, the Zond spacecraft was designed with cosmonauts in mind. The Zond missions served as test flights for the Soviet Union's plans to send cosmonauts to the moon. But those plans for crewed flights never came to fruition. This was partly because the U.S. had already put astronauts on the moon , but also because the Zond missions had a lot of technical problems. Zond 8 was considered a success — even though its guidance system malfunctioned on the way back to Earth.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos is playing the long game with Blue Origin (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: If Blue Origin goes public, it will have to meet the expectations of shareholders. Jeff Bezos may therefore want to establish a stronger business before committing to a listing.
articles.body: Daniel Biedermann is a partner at NewSpace Capital. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . Jeff Bezos , the founder and former CEO of Amazon, recently said that Blue Origin , his space technology company, is likely to go public in the coming years. The announcement has (unsurprisingly) attracted considerable attention, not least because Bezos has spent more than two decades financing the company largely from his personal wealth. He has invested billions of dollars in developing rockets , spacecraft and other forms of technology, often with very little prospect of an immediate return. But although Bezos has now raised the possibility of an initial public offering, he has given no firm indication of when one might happen.
articles.author: Daniel Biedermann
